## Simple explanation

An attention mechanism lets a neural network give different amounts of
importance to different parts of its input when producing a representation
or an output.

For example, when processing a sentence, a model may need to focus more on
some words than others to interpret a particular word.

## Technical explanation

In the Transformer formulation, scaled dot-product attention uses queries
(Q), keys (K), and values (V):

\[
\operatorname{Attention}(Q,K,V)
= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V
\]

The query-key dot products produce compatibility scores. Scaling helps
control their magnitude, softmax converts them into weights, and those
weights combine the value vectors.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Attention is a central building block in Transformer models used for
language, vision, audio, and multimodal tasks. Understanding it helps
engineers reason about model architecture, context length, computational
cost, and inference optimizations.

## How it works

1. Project input representations into queries, keys, and values.
2. Compare queries with keys to obtain relevance scores.
3. Scale the scores and apply softmax.
4. Use the resulting weights to combine value vectors.

Multi-head attention performs several attention operations in parallel,
allowing the model to learn different relationships.

## Practical example

The accompanying notebook demonstrates scaled dot-product attention using
small NumPy arrays. It is intended to make the tensor operations visible,
not to train a language model.

## Common misconceptions

- Attention weights are not automatically faithful explanations of a
  model's reasoning.
- Attention is not the same thing as memory.
- The original Transformer uses self-attention, but attention mechanisms
  also appear in other architectures.
